opis: The Rust language by topic: the core from „The Rust Programming Language“ and advanced chapters from Jon Gjengset's „Rust for Rustaceans“

pitanja.pitanje: By default, a variable declared with $let$ is…
pitanja.zanimljivost: Mutability is opt-in with $let mut$. The compiler even warns when you write $mut$ but never actually change the variable.

pitanja.pitanje: What does shadowing ($let x = …; let x = …;$) allow that $mut$ does not?
odgovori: Changing the type under the same name
pitanja.zanimljivost: The Book's example: $let spaces = "   "; let spaces = spaces.len();$ – the name stays, but the type changes from a string slice to a number.

pitanja.pitanje: Which integer type does Rust use when it cannot infer anything better?
pitanja.zanimljivost: $i32$ is usually the fastest choice even on 64-bit machines. For floating point, the default is $f64$.

pitanja.pitanje: In a debug build, what happens when a $u8$ holding 255 is increased by 1?
pitanja.zanimljivost: In release builds overflow checks are off by default and the value wraps. To choose explicitly, use $wrapping_add$, $checked_add$, $saturating_add$ or $overflowing_add$.

pitanja.pitanje: How many bytes does a Rust $char$ occupy?
pitanja.zanimljivost: A $char$ is a Unicode scalar value, so it can hold Cyrillic letters, Chinese characters and emoji – unlike a C $char$.

pitanja.pitanje: What is the value of $y$ here?
pitanja.zanimljivost: A block is an expression and its last line without a semicolon is its value. Add a semicolon after $x + 1$ and the block's value becomes $()$.

pitanja.pitanje: Which loop can return a value with $break value$?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Only $loop$ is guaranteed to end through a $break$, so only it can produce a value: $let r = loop { … break n * 2; };$

pitanja.pitanje: What must a $const$ declaration always have?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Constants are named in SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, e.g. $const SECONDS_IN_HOUR: u32 = 60 * 60;$ – the value must be computable at compile time.

pitanja.pitanje: What happens when you compile this?
pitanja.zanimljivost: $if$ is an expression, and every variable must have exactly one type known at compile time, so both branches must agree.

mediji.tekst:
let c = true;
let n = if c { 5 } else { "six" };

pitanja.pitanje: Match each type with its description
pitanja.zanimljivost: $usize$ is used for indexing collections because its size matches the machine's address width (64 bits on most computers today).

pitanja.pitanje: An array has 5 elements and the index comes from user input as 10. What happens on $a[i]$?
odgovori: A panic: index out of bounds
It silently reads memory past the end
pitanja.zanimljivost: Rust checks bounds at run time, which is exactly what C does not do. If you want to handle it yourself, $a.get(i)$ returns an $Option$.

pitanja.pitanje: Given $let t = (500, 6.4, 1);$, what is $t.1$?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Tuple fields are indexed from zero with a dot. The empty tuple $()$ is called the unit type – what a function returns when it returns “nothing”.

pitanja.pitanje: What does this print?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Each $let$ creates a brand-new variable that shadows the old one. The inner $x$ disappears at the closing brace, so the outer $x$ (6) is visible again. Shadowing can even change the type: $let s = s.len();$ is fine.

pitanja.pitanje: What does this print?
pitanja.zanimljivost: $wrapping_add$ wraps around modulo 256, so 260 becomes 4. Plain $+$ would panic in a debug build and wrap in release; $checked_add$ returns $None$ and $saturating_add$ stops at 255.

mediji.tekst:
let x: u8 = 250;
println!("{}", x.wrapping_add(10));

pitanja.pitanje: How many owners can a value have at one time?
pitanja.zanimljivost: The three rules: every value has an owner, there is only one owner at a time, and the value is dropped when the owner goes out of scope.

pitanja.pitanje: What happens on the last line?
odgovori: It prints an empty string after the move
pitanja.zanimljivost: Copying only the pointer would make two owners free the same memory (a double free). Rust instead moves ownership and invalidates $s1$.

pitanja.pitanje: Why can you still use $x$ after $let x = 5; let y = x;$?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Types whose size is known and that own no other resources (integers, $bool$, $char$, floats, tuples of such) are copied bit by bit.

pitanja.pitanje: What do the borrowing rules allow at any given time?
odgovori: One mutable or many shared references
Many mutable and many shared references
One mutable plus one shared reference
pitanja.zanimljivost: It is like a reading room: many people may read a book at once, but whoever writes in it must be alone.

pitanja.pitanje: Which bug class does the “one mutable reference” rule prevent at compile time?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Surprisingly, leaks are NOT prevented: $std::mem::forget$ is a safe function, and $Rc$ cycles can leak memory.

pitanja.pitanje: What does the compiler say about this function?
odgovori: It moves $s$ to the heap automatically
pitanja.zanimljivost: $s$ is dropped at the end of the function, so the reference would dangle. The fix is to return the $String$ itself and move ownership out.

pitanja.pitanje: What is a string slice ($&str$)?
odgovori: A pointer and length into UTF-8 text
An array of $char$ on the stack
pitanja.zanimljivost: That's why a function taking $&str$ accepts both literals and $&String$: the $String$ derefs to a slice of itself.

pitanja.pitanje: What is the type of the literal $"hello"$?
pitanja.zanimljivost: The bytes of the literal are stored directly in the program's binary, so the reference stays valid for the whole run.

pitanja.pitanje: When is a $String$'s heap memory freed?
odgovori: When its owner goes out of scope
When the garbage collector next runs
pitanja.zanimljivost: At the closing brace Rust automatically calls $drop$. The pattern is known from C++ as RAII.

pitanja.pitanje: Does this compile?
odgovori: Yes – $r1$ is not used after printing
pitanja.zanimljivost: Since the 2018 edition, Non-Lexical Lifetimes end a borrow at its last use, not at the end of the block.

pitanja.pitanje: Match each type with what it means
pitanja.zanimljivost: “Shared” and “exclusive” are better names than “immutable” and “mutable” – some types allow mutation even through $&T$ (interior mutability).

pitanja.pitanje: Which of these types does NOT implement $Copy$?
pitanja.objasnjenje: $String$ owns memory on the heap; copying it bit by bit would create two owners. You must call $.clone()$ explicitly.
pitanja.zanimljivost: A type cannot implement both $Copy$ and $Drop$ – if a type needs cleanup, a silent copy would be dangerous.

pitanja.pitanje: What happens on the last line?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Passing a $String$ by value moves it into the function, which drops it at its end. Pass $&s$ instead to only borrow it, or call $s.clone()$ if the function really needs its own copy.

pitanja.pitanje: Does this compile, and what does it print?
pitanja.zanimljivost: $i32$ implements $Copy$, so $let b = a;$ copies the bits and $a$ stays usable. $String$ owns heap memory and isn't $Copy$ – without $.clone()$ the second line would move it.

pitanja.pitanje: When does the shorthand $User { email, username }$ work?
odgovori: Variables have the same names as fields
pitanja.zanimljivost: It's called field init shorthand – it saves you from writing $email: email$.

pitanja.pitanje: $username$ is a $String$. What about $u1$ after this?
odgovori: It can't be used as a whole anymore
It is unchanged and fully usable
It is always a compile error
pitanja.zanimljivost: Struct update syntax moves the remaining fields. $u1.email$ is still usable, but $u1$ as a whole is not, because $username$ moved.

pitanja.pitanje: Which line declares a tuple struct?
pitanja.zanimljivost: $Color$ and $Point(i32, i32, i32)$ are different types even with the same fields – that is the point of naming them.

pitanja.pitanje: What is a unit-like struct such as $struct AlwaysEqual;$ useful for?
odgovori: Implementing a trait with no data
Creating a global variable with no type
pitanja.zanimljivost: It takes zero bytes of memory. Marker types like this are common in typestate APIs.

pitanja.pitanje: Which derive lets you print a struct with $\{:?\}$?
pitanja.zanimljivost: $\{:#?\}$ pretty-prints, and $dbg!(expr)$ prints file, line and value to stderr – and returns ownership of the value.

pitanja.pitanje: In a method signature, $&self$ is short for…
pitanja.zanimljivost: $Self$ is an alias for the type the $impl$ block is for. Methods may also take $self: Box<Self>$ or $self: Rc<Self>$.

pitanja.pitanje: How do you call an associated function that has no $self$, like $from$?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Constructors such as $new$ are ordinary associated functions – Rust has no special constructor syntax.

pitanja.pitanje: Why can you write $p1.distance(&p2)$ instead of $(&p1).distance(&p2)$?
odgovori: Methods always take ownership of $p1$ anyway
pitanja.zanimljivost: Automatic referencing works because the receiver's type is clear from the method signature. C++ needs separate $.$ and $->$ operators.

pitanja.pitanje: How many $impl$ blocks can one struct have?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Splitting methods into several $impl$ blocks is useful with generics: $impl Point<f32>$ adds methods only for one concrete type.

pitanja.pitanje: Why does the Book's $User$ struct store $String$ rather than $&str$?
odgovori: Each instance owns all its data
Structs can't hold references of any kind
pitanja.zanimljivost: Storing references is allowed, but then the struct needs lifetime parameters – a topic the Book postpones to chapter 10.

pitanja.pitanje: Match the method receiver with what the method can do
pitanja.zanimljivost: Methods taking $self$ are rare; they typically turn the value into something else, like $String::into_bytes$.

pitanja.pitanje: Why doesn't this compile?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Calling $c.inc()$ auto-borrows $&mut c$, which needs a mutable binding: $let mut c = …$. Mutability in Rust belongs to the binding, not to individual fields of a struct.

pitanja.pitanje: What does this print?
pitanja.zanimljivost: $#[derive(Debug)]$ writes the formatting code for you. With ${:#?}$ you get a pretty, multi-line version – handy for big nested structs.

pitanja.pitanje: What does Rust use instead of null?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Tony Hoare called null his “billion-dollar mistake”. With $Option$ the compiler forces you to handle the missing case.

pitanja.pitanje: What are the variants of $Option<T>$?
pitanja.zanimljivost: They are in the prelude, so you write $Some(5)$ instead of $Option::Some(5)$.

pitanja.pitanje: What happens if a $match$ on an enum leaves out one variant?
odgovori: A panic when it is hit
pitanja.zanimljivost: Exhaustiveness checking pays off when you add a variant later: the compiler lists every $match$ you forgot to update.

pitanja.pitanje: What is $if let Some(x) = opt { … }$?
odgovori: A declaration of $x$ as a global variable
pitanja.zanimljivost: You trade exhaustiveness for brevity. An $else$ branch plays the role of $_ =>$ in $match$.

pitanja.pitanje: How does the catch-all $_$ differ from a named pattern like $other$?
pitanja.zanimljivost: $_ => ()$ is the idiom for “do nothing in all other cases”.

pitanja.pitanje: What can enum variants hold?
odgovori: Data of one shared type for all variants
pitanja.zanimljivost: $enum Message { Quit, Move { x: i32, y: i32 }, Write(String) }$ – one type, variants shaped differently.

pitanja.pitanje: With $x = Some(5)$, what does this $match$ return?
pitanja.zanimljivost: A match guard ($if n > 5$) is checked after the pattern matches. The compiler does not use guards when checking exhaustiveness.

pitanja.pitanje: In the pattern $id @ 3..=7$, what does $@$ do?
odgovori: Binds the value while testing it
Marks the whole pattern as optional
pitanja.zanimljivost: Without $@$ you could test the range, but you wouldn't have the actual number in a variable.

pitanja.pitanje: In $let Some(x) = opt else { … };$ what must the $else$ block do?
pitanja.zanimljivost: let-else (stable since Rust 1.65) keeps the “happy path” unindented, which is great for early returns.

pitanja.pitanje: When does $while let Some(top) = stack.pop()$ stop?
pitanja.zanimljivost: $pop$ on a $Vec$ returns $Option<T>$, which makes it a natural fit for $while let$.

pitanja.pitanje: Which pattern is refutable, so a plain $let$ rejects it?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Refutable patterns can fail to match. $let$, function parameters and $for$ loops accept only irrefutable ones.

pitanja.pitanje: Match each pattern with its meaning
pitanja.zanimljivost: Ranges in patterns work only for numbers and $char$, because the compiler must check if the range is empty.

pitanja.pitanje: What is $s$?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Arms are tried top to bottom. 7 is outside $3..=6$, so the match guard $if x % 2 == 1$ decides. The compiler can't reason about guards, which is why the $_$ arm is still required.

pitanja.pitanje: What is $b$?
pitanja.zanimljivost: $map$ on $None$ does nothing and stays $None$, so $unwrap_or$ gives the fallback. If computing the fallback is expensive, $unwrap_or_else(|| …)$ only runs it when needed.

mediji.tekst:
let a: Option<i32> = None;
let b = a.map(|x| x * 2).unwrap_or(10);

pitanja.pitanje: What is a crate?
odgovori: The smallest unit the compiler builds
A folder that contains only the test files
pitanja.zanimljivost: A crate is either a binary (has $main$) or a library. In everyday speech Rustaceans often say crate when they mean a library.

pitanja.pitanje: Which file is the crate root of a library crate by default?
pitanja.zanimljivost: If a package has both $src/main.rs$ and $src/lib.rs$, it contains two crates with the same name.

pitanja.pitanje: By default, an item inside a module is…
odgovori: Private to its module and children
Private to the file it is written in
pitanja.zanimljivost: Child modules can see their ancestors' private items, but parents can't see into private children.

pitanja.pitanje: If a struct is $pub$, what about its fields?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Enums are the opposite: if the enum is $pub$, all its variants are public too.

pitanja.pitanje: What does $use std::io::Result as IoResult;$ do?
odgovori: Brings the type in under a new name
Re-exports it publicly from your crate
pitanja.zanimljivost: $as$ solves name clashes, e.g. between $fmt::Result$ and $io::Result$.

pitanja.pitanje: What is $pub use$ for?
pitanja.zanimljivost: It lets the public API differ from the internal module tree – users write $mycrate::Thing$ instead of a long path.

pitanja.pitanje: What is $Cargo.lock$ for?
odgovori: Preventing two builds from running at once
pitanja.zanimljivost: Binaries should commit it to version control so everyone builds the same thing. Cargo now recommends committing it for libraries too.

pitanja.pitanje: What $opt-level$ does the release profile use by default?
pitanja.zanimljivost: The dev profile uses $opt-level = 0$ – faster compilation, slower code. $"s"$ and $"z"$ optimize for size.

pitanja.pitanje: Match each path start with what it refers to
pitanja.zanimljivost: $super$ works like $..$ in a file system path.

pitanja.pitanje: What do packages in a Cargo workspace share?
odgovori: One common $main$ function for all crates
pitanja.zanimljivost: Sharing the $target$ directory avoids rebuilding the same dependencies for each crate in the workspace.

pitanja.pitanje: How many library crates can one package contain?
pitanja.zanimljivost: But it can have many binary crates: each file in $src/bin/$ becomes a separate binary.

pitanja.pitanje: Which comment style becomes HTML documentation for the next item?
pitanja.zanimljivost: $//!$ documents the enclosing item (usually the whole crate). Code examples in doc comments are run as tests.

pitanja.pitanje: Why doesn't this compile outside module $shop$?
pitanja.zanimljivost: A $pub struct$ doesn't make its fields public – each one needs its own $pub$. With a private field, outsiders can only build the struct through a function like $Item::new$, which keeps invariants safe.

pitanja.pitanje: Which macro creates a $Vec$ with given elements?
pitanja.zanimljivost: $vec![0; 5]$ creates five zeros – the same syntax as array repeat expressions.

pitanja.pitanje: For a 5-element vector $v$, how do $v.get(100)$ and $&v[100]$ differ?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Choose based on whether an out-of-range index is a bug ($[]$) or a normal situation ($get$).

pitanja.pitanje: Why doesn't this compile?
pitanja.zanimljivost: If the vector has no spare capacity, $push$ allocates a new buffer and copies elements – $first$ would point to freed memory.

pitanja.pitanje: Why can't you write $s[0]$ on a $String$?
odgovori: A byte is not always a character
Strings are always immutable in Rust
pitanja.zanimljivost: Indexing is expected to be O(1), but finding the n-th character in UTF-8 requires walking from the start.

pitanja.pitanje: What does $"Здраво".len()$ return?
pitanja.zanimljivost: $len()$ counts bytes, and every Cyrillic letter takes 2 bytes in UTF-8. $.chars().count()$ would return 6.

pitanja.pitanje: After $let s3 = s1 + &s2;$, which strings can you still use?
pitanja.zanimljivost: $+$ calls $add(self, s: &str)$: it takes ownership of $s1$, appends to its buffer and returns it. $format!$ doesn't take ownership of anything.

pitanja.pitanje: What does this loop compute?
odgovori: Counts how often each word occurs
Inserts each word only once, never again
pitanja.zanimljivost: $or_insert$ returns $&mut V$ to the existing or newly inserted value – a classic word counter in one line.

pitanja.pitanje: Which hash function does $HashMap$ use by default?
pitanja.zanimljivost: SipHash is not the fastest, but resists HashDoS attacks. You can swap in another hasher with the $BuildHasher$ trait.

pitanja.pitanje: What happens to a $String$ key inserted into a $HashMap$?
odgovori: The map takes ownership of it
The map stores a reference to the key
pitanja.zanimljivost: If you insert references instead, the referenced values must outlive the map.

pitanja.pitanje: Which of these is NOT a Rust standard library collection?
pitanja.objasnjenje: $ArrayList$ is Java's growable array; in Rust that role is played by $Vec$.
pitanja.zanimljivost: $std::collections$ docs advise: “use $Vec$ or $HashMap$” for almost everything.

pitanja.pitanje: Match each collection with its role
pitanja.zanimljivost: $BTreeMap$ is a B-tree, not a binary tree – each node holds several keys, which is friendlier to CPU caches.

pitanja.pitanje: How many $char$ values are in the Hindi word “नमस्ते”?
pitanja.zanimljivost: The Book's example: 18 bytes, 6 Unicode scalar values, but 4 letters (grapheme clusters) as a reader would count them.

pitanja.pitanje: Why doesn't this compile?
pitanja.zanimljivost: $push$ may reallocate the buffer and move every element, which would leave $first$ pointing at freed memory. In C++ this is the classic „iterator invalidation“ bug; Rust rejects it at compile time.

pitanja.pitanje: What does this print?
pitanja.zanimljivost: $len$ counts bytes, not letters. Each Cyrillic letter takes 2 bytes in UTF-8, so 6 letters are 12 bytes. $s.chars().count()$ gives 6. That's also why $s[0]$ doesn't compile.

mediji.tekst:
let s = String::from("здраво");
println!("{}", s.len());

pitanja.pitanje: Which macro signals an unrecoverable error?
pitanja.zanimljivost: By default, a panic unwinds the stack and runs destructors. Rust has no exceptions in the usual sense.

pitanja.pitanje: What are the variants of $Result<T, E>$?
pitanja.zanimljivost: $Result$ is marked $#[must_use]$ – ignoring one produces a compiler warning.

pitanja.pitanje: What does $?$ do when the value is $Err(e)$?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Conversion goes through the $From$ trait, so one function can turn many error types into its own.

pitanja.pitanje: In which functions can you use the $?$ operator?
pitanja.zanimljivost: More precisely: types implementing $FromResidual$. You can't mix them – $?$ on an $Option$ in a function returning $Result$ won't compile.

pitanja.pitanje: How does $expect("msg")$ differ from $unwrap()$?
odgovori: It returns a default value instead
pitanja.zanimljivost: Many Rustaceans write the message as the expectation: $expect("config file should exist")$.

pitanja.pitanje: What does $panic = 'abort'$ in a Cargo profile change?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Without unwinding there's no need for cleanup tables in the binary, but destructors of other values won't run.

pitanja.pitanje: If $main$ returns $Err$, the process exits with…
pitanja.zanimljivost: $main$ can return any type implementing $Termination$, e.g. $Result<(), Box<dyn Error>>$.

pitanja.pitanje: Which environment variable shows a backtrace on panic?
pitanja.zanimljivost: $RUST_BACKTRACE=full$ shows even more frames. Line numbers need debug symbols, which are on in debug builds.

pitanja.pitanje: When does the Book consider $unwrap$ acceptable?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Also when you know more than the compiler, e.g. parsing the hard-coded IP address $"127.0.0.1"$.

pitanja.pitanje: What does $"42".parse::<i32>()$ return?
pitanja.zanimljivost: $parse$ is generic over any type implementing $FromStr$, so you must say which type you want.

pitanja.pitanje: Match each method with what it does
pitanja.zanimljivost: $unwrap_or_else(f)$ computes the default lazily – only when it is actually needed.

pitanja.pitanje: What does the Book's $Guess$ type (accepting only 1–100) illustrate?
odgovori: Using a type to guarantee validity
Using panics for normal control flow
pitanja.zanimljivost: Once checked in $Guess::new$, the value can't be invalid, so other functions need no repeated checks.

pitanja.pitanje: What do $parse(" 21 ")$ and $parse("x")$ return?
pitanja.zanimljivost: $?$ returns the error early from the function instead of panicking. It also calls $From::from$ on the error, so one function can bubble up several error types into one.

pitanja.pitanje: What is a trait?
odgovori: A class with its own fields and inheritance
pitanja.zanimljivost: Traits resemble interfaces in other languages, but you can implement your trait even for types you didn't write, like $i32$.

pitanja.pitanje: Can your crate implement $Display$ for $Vec<T>$?
odgovori: Yes, but only inside an $unsafe$ block
pitanja.zanimljivost: The orphan rule ensures two crates can't provide conflicting implementations. The workaround is a newtype wrapper.

pitanja.pitanje: Why do Rust generics cost nothing at run time?
pitanja.zanimljivost: The compiler generates a separate copy of the code for each concrete type – fast, but it makes binaries larger.

pitanja.pitanje: $fn notify(item: &impl Summary)$ is shorthand for…
odgovori: A generic with a trait bound
pitanja.zanimljivost: The long form is $fn notify<T: Summary>(item: &T)$. Only the long form can force two parameters to be the same type.

pitanja.pitanje: What is a $where$ clause for?
odgovori: Choosing which branch runs at run time

mediji.tekst:
fn f<T, U>(t: &T, u: &U) -> i32
where
    T: Display + Clone,
    U: Clone + Debug,
{ … }

pitanja.zanimljivost: Long bound lists in angle brackets get hard to read; $where$ moves them after the signature.

pitanja.pitanje: A function returns $impl Summary$. What may it return?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Returning a $Tweet$ in one branch and a $NewsArticle$ in another won't compile – for that you need $Box<dyn Summary>$.

pitanja.pitanje: What happens with a default method implementation in a trait?
odgovori: Types may use or override it
Every implementing type must override it
pitanja.zanimljivost: A default method may call other methods of the same trait that have no default – a type implements just a little and gets a lot.

pitanja.pitanje: What is $impl<T: Display> ToString for T$ an example of?
pitanja.zanimljivost: That's why you can call $.to_string()$ on any type that implements $Display$.

pitanja.pitanje: Why does $fn largest<T: PartialOrd>(list: &[T]) -> &T$ need $PartialOrd$?
odgovori: To hash the items for lookups
pitanja.zanimljivost: “Partial” because some values are incomparable – for floats, $NaN$ isn't less, greater or equal to anything.

pitanja.pitanje: Match each derivable trait with what it gives you
pitanja.zanimljivost: A $HashMap$ key needs $Eq$ as well as $Hash$, and equal values must have equal hashes.

pitanja.pitanje: What does $impl Point<f32> { fn distance_from_origin(&self) … }$ mean?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Methods can be added for one concrete type, while the rest of the $impl<T>$ block is shared by all $Point<T>$.

pitanja.pitanje: What does the compiler say about $p$?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Both fields share one $T$. For different types, declare $Point<T, U>$.

pitanja.pitanje: What does this print?
pitanja.zanimljivost: $greet$ has a default body, so implementors only have to write $name$. A default method may call required ones – a pattern similar to the „template method“ from OOP.

pitanja.pitanje: What is the main purpose of lifetimes?
odgovori: Measuring how long code takes to run
pitanja.zanimljivost: Most lifetimes are inferred, just like most types. You annotate them only where the compiler can't decide.

pitanja.pitanje: In $fn longest<'a>(x: &'a str, y: &'a str) -> &'a str$, how long is the result valid?
odgovori: As long as the shorter-lived input
As long as the longer-lived of the two inputs
pitanja.zanimljivost: $'a$ becomes the overlap of both inputs' lifetimes, so the result is safe whichever one is returned.

pitanja.pitanje: According to the elision rules, when there is exactly one input lifetime…
odgovori: It's assigned to all output references
The output gets a new, separate lifetime
pitanja.zanimljivost: Rule 1: every input reference gets its own lifetime. Rule 2: a single input lifetime goes to outputs. Rule 3: with $&self$, outputs get $self$'s lifetime.

pitanja.pitanje: For a method taking $&self$ and another reference, which lifetime does the returned reference get?
pitanja.zanimljivost: It's the third elision rule – the reason most methods need no lifetime annotations at all.

pitanja.pitanje: What does $'static$ mean on a reference?
odgovori: It can live for the whole program
pitanja.zanimljivost: When the compiler suggests $'static$, it's often a sign of a different problem, such as a dangling reference.

pitanja.pitanje: What does $struct Excerpt<'a> { part: &'a str }$ guarantee?
odgovori: An instance can't outlive the text
The struct must always live on the heap
pitanja.zanimljivost: The Book splits a novel into sentences – each $Excerpt$ only points into the original text.

pitanja.pitanje: What does the compiler say here?
pitanja.zanimljivost: The borrow checker compares scopes: $x$ dies at the inner closing brace, but $r$ is still used afterwards.

pitanja.pitanje: Do lifetime annotations change how long references live?
odgovori: Yes – they extend how long values live
pitanja.zanimljivost: Annotations are a contract checked by the compiler, not an instruction for it. They never make a value live longer.

pitanja.pitanje: How are lifetime parameters written?
odgovori: An apostrophe and a short name
A dollar sign and a name
pitanja.zanimljivost: Usually $'a$, $'b$… The special $'_$ means “let the compiler infer it”.

pitanja.pitanje: What does the bound $T: 'static$ mean?
odgovori: $T$ must be declared as a $static$ item
pitanja.zanimljivost: A $String$ satisfies $T: 'static$ – it owns its data. That's why $thread::spawn$ accepts owned values.

pitanja.pitanje: Match each type with its description
parovi: Text valid for the whole run
pitanja.zanimljivost: The lifetime always comes right after the $&$ and before $mut$.

pitanja.pitanje: Why doesn't this compile?
pitanja.zanimljivost: The borrow checker compares scopes: $x$ dies at the closing brace while $r$ is used after it. A reference must never outlive what it points to – that's what lifetimes describe.

pitanja.pitanje: Which attribute marks a function as a test?
pitanja.zanimljivost: A test fails if it panics. $cargo test$ builds a special binary that runs all marked functions.

pitanja.pitanje: What does $assert_eq!(a, b)$ add over $assert!(a == b)$?
odgovori: It prints both values on failure
It also compares the types of both values
pitanja.zanimljivost: Both values must implement $PartialEq$ and $Debug$. In Rust the order of “left” and “right” doesn't matter.

pitanja.pitanje: What does $#[should_panic(expected = "less than 100")]$ check?
odgovori: The panic message contains that text
The test panics before printing anything
pitanja.zanimljivost: $expected$ makes the test more precise – it fails if the code panics for some other reason.

pitanja.pitanje: How does $cargo test$ run tests by default?
pitanja.zanimljivost: If tests share state (e.g. a file), run $cargo test -- --test-threads=1$.

pitanja.pitanje: What happens to $println!$ output from a passing test?
odgovori: It goes to a log file
It causes the test to fail
pitanja.zanimljivost: $cargo test -- --show-output$ shows output from passing tests too.

pitanja.pitanje: How do you run only the tests marked $#[ignore]$?
pitanja.zanimljivost: $--include-ignored$ runs both kinds. Ignoring is meant for slow tests, not broken ones.

pitanja.pitanje: Why are unit tests put in a $#[cfg(test)] mod tests$?
pitanja.zanimljivost: So the test code doesn't end up in the final binary and doesn't slow down $cargo build$.

pitanja.pitanje: Where do integration tests go, and what can they use?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Each file in $tests/$ is compiled as a separate crate. Shared helpers go in $tests/common/mod.rs$.

pitanja.pitanje: Can unit tests call private functions?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Some languages forbid testing private functions; Rust allows it because the test module is a child module.

pitanja.pitanje: What does a test returning $Result<(), String>$ allow?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Such a test fails when it returns $Err$. It can't be combined with $#[should_panic]$.

pitanja.pitanje: Why do binary projects keep most logic in $src/lib.rs$?
odgovori: Cargo needs at least one library crate per package
pitanja.zanimljivost: A thin $main.rs$ that calls the library is the pattern the Book uses for its $minigrep$ project.

pitanja.pitanje: How do you run this test?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Arguments after $--$ go to the test binary, not to Cargo. $-- --include-ignored$ runs both normal and ignored tests in one go.

pitanja.pitanje: Which is a closure that adds one?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Closures can capture variables from their environment – that's what separates them from ordinary functions.

pitanja.pitanje: Match each closure trait or keyword with what it allows
pitanja.zanimljivost: Every closure implements $FnOnce$. A closure that's $Fn$ is also $FnMut$ and $FnOnce$.

pitanja.pitanje: Why do closures passed to $thread::spawn$ usually need $move$?
odgovori: The thread may outlive the variables
pitanja.zanimljivost: Without $move$, the closure would borrow from a stack frame that could disappear before the thread finishes.

pitanja.pitanje: What does $v.iter().map(|x| x + 1);$ do on its own?
odgovori: Adds 1 to every element of $v$ in place
pitanja.zanimljivost: The compiler even warns: “unused $Map$ that must be used – iterators are lazy and do nothing unless consumed”.

pitanja.pitanje: Match each method with what the iterator yields
pitanja.zanimljivost: $for x in &v$ calls $iter()$, and $for x in v$ calls $into_iter()$ and consumes the vector.

pitanja.pitanje: Which method must you implement for the $Iterator$ trait?
pitanja.zanimljivost: All the dozens of other methods ($map$, $filter$, $zip$…) have default implementations built on $next$.

pitanja.pitanje: What is the $::<>$ syntax in $collect::<Vec<_>>()$ called?
pitanja.zanimljivost: The name was coined by Anna Harren in 2015. The Rust parser's test suite has a test called “bastion of the turbofish”.

pitanja.pitanje: How does iterator code compare to a hand-written loop in speed?
pitanja.zanimljivost: In the Book's benchmark the iterator version was even slightly faster; the compiler unrolls loops and removes bounds checks.

pitanja.pitanje: After $let total: i32 = it.sum();$, can you use $it$ again?
odgovori: Only if it was declared mutable
pitanja.zanimljivost: Methods that call $next$ until the end are called consuming adapters.

pitanja.pitanje: What is $(1..4).map(|x| x * x).sum::<i32>()$?
pitanja.zanimljivost: $1..4$ excludes the upper bound: 1 + 4 + 9 = 14. With $1..=4$ the result would be 30.

pitanja.pitanje: What happens here?
odgovori: Type error on the second call
It works and returns $5$ the second time
pitanja.zanimljivost: A closure's parameter types are inferred from its first use and then fixed. Closures are not generic.

pitanja.pitanje: What does this print?
pitanja.zanimljivost: Iterator adapters are lazy: $map$ only builds a new iterator, and nothing calls $next$ on it. The compiler warns „unused $Map$ that must be used“. Use a $for$ loop or $for_each$ for side effects.
